subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should user-configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys that match credential patterns be allowed to reach host exec subprocesses when the skill metadata does not declare them?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but changing it decides a credential-to-exec security boundary rather than a purely mechanical propagation bug.

options.title: Allow explicit per-skill config keys
options.body: Treat keys explicitly configured under a skill entry as operator intent, keep the hard dangerous-env denylist, and require regression/redaction tests for credential-shaped names.

options.title: Require skill metadata declarations
options.body: Keep current blocking behavior unless the skill declares the env key in metadata, and update docs/error messaging so users know how to make a key eligible.

options.title: Defer to a broader secrets design
options.body: Leave this issue blocked until a wider SecretRef or sandbox-env contract settles credential delivery to executable tools.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit per-skill config keys
recommendation.body: Treat keys explicitly configured under a skill entry as operator intent, keep the hard dangerous-env denylist, and require regression/redaction tests for credential-shaped names.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest current-main ownership of the skill-env override implementation and its regression fixes.
